Paragraph: "He who gave away riches in charity, who obtained unequalled renown and who himself was the lord of this world earlier, now accepts the lordship of Sugreeva...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Highlighting Rama's supreme humility despite his royal stature.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Pointing out that despite past glory, Rama is humble enough to seek a friend and leader in Sugreeva.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Ego: Humility, absence of false pride despite past greatness

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Nirahamkara (absence of ego and false pride)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Rama's willingness to seek help reflects total nirahamkara (ego-transcendence).
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Demonstrates emotional maturity: the ability to set aside status and ego when seeking necessary collaboration.
